scope: Real customer feedback led to a client-private strategy revision, retrieved during a second paid execution with identical scope/input. The actual generated CSS accent changed to the customer preference. This demonstrates persisted memory/strategy adaptation, not model-weight training or a controlled causal evaluation.

evaluation.feedback: For my future Hearth & Grain website work, please use exactly #375E70 as the actual CSS accent color. This is my brand preference after reviewing the previous artifact. Also supply the final visitor-facing About, Catering Services and How It Works copy, rather than instructions for assembling a website. Keep supplied facts and missing-contact constraints unchanged.

strategy.guidance: For all future Hearth & Grain website work: set the CSS accent color exactly to #375E70 on real elements (headings, links, borders, small decorative blocks) instead of the previous muted terracotta — contrast must remain accessible, so use the accent for large/bold text or darken it for small text on the neutral background. Deliverables are complete visitor-facing sections, not assembly instructions: final About, Catering Services and How It Works copy drawn only from client-supplied facts (About = seasonal catering for neighborhood gatherings; Catering Services = menu planning and procurement comparisons; How It Works = customers first share guest count, event date and dietary constraints). No invented emails, addresses, order forms, testimonials, pricing, photos, scripts, remote assets, payments, checkout, hosting or fulfillment claims; three sections only, no extra CTAs. Keep semantic headings, CSS-only responsive layout, HTML + CSS files previewable locally, no hosting/domains/photography/collaborators/future updates.
